report.text:
Task #18 done, commit 5817ec69e on team/33fbafeb/core (base dcea65962). Qt tests written but NOT run: this computer has no Qt 6 SDK (see Not checked).

Causes:
1. Create did nothing (decisive, matches your journal facts 13199/13200). With 7 members over max_members 6, the form disabled Create itself (TeamNewTab::validate: m_members.size() > m_max). hgs's preflight (plan::validate) reported the limit only as a warning, and the draft create (ops::draft "create") refuses only preflight errors. So the footer read "Preflight: ok · N warnings" beside a disabled button whose only hint was the small reason label. Removing one member lifted the form's block, and the next event was draft_created.
2. Lead edits could be skipped. applyDraft showed fields only when the read's revision differed from m_revision, the revision the form sends. The form's own save (draft_revision) and a stale refusal ("Draft revision is N now") both moved m_revision onto revisions it never read. So the lead's edits made in between (name/goal/members/tasks/settings) never reached the open form until the lead edited again. readDraft also dropped every read while a save was in flight, and the "kept" line vanished on the next poll.
3. Refusals were not clearly visible: a refused create was written into the save line as "Not saved: ...", and a failed read was silent.
Not the cause: the form's save payload. The new Rust test sends it exactly as the form does and hgs accepts it. The draft also binds correctly when started outside the form (openDraft from updateTeamPanel).

Changes:
- src/state/teams/plan.rs: more members than max_members is a preflight error (kind members), so Preflight, plan approval and draft create all refuse it the same way. docs/reference.md says so.
- tray/src/TeamNewTab.{h,cpp}: m_appliedRevision (last shown) apart from m_revision (to send). Every unread revision applies all fields the owner is not editing; text compares ignore surrounding whitespace so a just-saved field does not jump. Reads run during a save. Fields kept for the owner stay named until saved.
- Footer, one line each: "Not created: <reason>" (separate m_createError; a save failing under Create says "the draft did not save first: ..."), "Not saved (<fields>): <error>", "The lead's edits cannot be read: <error>".
- A save with no answer ends after 30 s, says so and is sent again.
- New "Show the lead's version" button: drops the owner's unsaved fields and rereads.
- Tests: Rust ops_members::a_draft_over_its_member_limit_is_refused_at_create_and_by_the_preflight (the form's first save accepted; over the limit is an error and create is refused naming it; one member fewer creates). plan.rs unit test updated (members moves from warnings to errors). Qt test_teamsui_newteam: draftShowsEveryLeadEditAroundTheOwnersSave (draft started outside the form opens with all fields; a lead edit updates name, goal, addendum, members, tasks and settings; the stale-refusal-then-save case shows the lead's newer goal), draftRefusedSaveKeepsTheOwnersFieldAndSaysSo, draftCreateRefusalAndMemberLimitAreShown. The fake hgs (TeamsUiFixture.h) gains .draftrefuse/.createrefuse.

report.text:
Task #20 done. Commit 4f8628a66 on team/33fbafeb/ui1. It is on top of task #3's commit 6b4ff06c5, whose parent is dcea65962. Nothing pushed.

Cause (the step that ran out)
- In src/state/worktrees.rs create(), the clone path ran `git clone` with its own deadline: 300 s, capped by the 315 s total. But the next steps, `git switch -c <branch> <head>` and the `symbolic-ref` confirmation, reused `deadline`. That deadline is `total_deadline.min(now + 5 s)`, computed BEFORE the clone. Once a clone took longer than about 5 s, switch failed at once with "Git operation cancelled or timed out". Clones of C:\work\example"not this member's folder".

Did an earlier fix regress?
- No. The stale deadline has been there since the clone code was added (c96b63273, 2026-10-26, "Fork: ... clones"). No branch in this repository has a different clone/switch deadline: I checked fix/team-setup-feedback, agent-teams-v2, int-fe2, integrate/upstream-2026-11-04 and whitewh/main.
- U34 (a4f54ac3a, 9d239e298, bb0a13732) is about the DeepSeek sandbox ACL grant (WRITE_DAC/WRITE_OWNER). All three commits are ancestors of this branch, and grant_if_requested is called after the clone as before. So U34 was not lost, and it covers a different failure. The owner's "we already fixed this" most likely means U34. If they mean a different fix, it is not in this repository's history.

What changed
- src/state/worktrees.rs create --clone:
  - Each step has its own deadline: clone 25 min (CLONE_SECONDS), base fetch plus switch 10 min (CHECKOUT_SECONDS), confirmation 30 s. Mobile requests keep their 25 s total.
  - A destination that exists is finished instead of refused, but only if unfinished_clone() confirms it: it is a folder whose own toplevel and .git are the clone's own, its origin is this repository, refs/heads/<branch> does not exist, and `status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` is empty. If the base commit is missing (the base moved on after the clone), `git fetch origin` runs first. Anything else is still refused with the reason and never changed. A failure now says the clone is kept and that starting the member again finishes it.
  - The result carries "resumed".
  - I kept `--no-hardlinks` and did not use --shared or --reference. On Windows, a hard link shares the source file's ACL, so the U34 inheritable FullControl grant would reach the lead's repository. A --shared clone depends on the source's objects through alternates (gc/prune) and on the sandbox being able to read them.
- src/state/teams/dispatcher.rs:
  - The member branch starts from team.settings.base_branch when set, else from HEAD of the team folder (the lead's branch, as before). This also applies to worktree members.
  - A local clone member's folder that is a clone of the team repository without the member's branch goes back to `worktrees create`. A remote clone member on another branch does too. A worktree member and foreign folders are still refused.
  - The hgs call for `worktrees create` may take 40 min; the catalog reads keep 5 min.
  - Note: launch() calls member_folder synchronously, as before. A slow clone holds that launch for its duration, as the 300 s timeout already did.
- docs/reference.md: a new "Members' clones" paragraph next to the DeepSeek folders section.

Tests
- state::worktrees::tests::a_slow_clone_finishes_on_the_base_branch: a test hook sleeps 6 s after `git clone`, past the old 5 s window. Setup completes on team/x/dev at the `base` branch's commit, not main's, and b.txt is checked out.
- state::worktrees::tests::an_unfinished_clone_is_finished_on_relaunch: a leftover clone on main.
  - With a local change: refused and left untouched.
  - Clean: finished, the base that moved on is fetched, HEAD is the new base commit, resumed=true.
  - A second create: refused ("its branch exists already").
  - Another repository at the destination: refused.
- dispatcher_worktrees::an_unfinished_clone_member_is_finished_from_the_base_branch: the leftover clone is handed to create with --clone --base release; with no base_branch the base is HEAD; a finished clone is reused with no call.

How I checked
- cargo-test --bin hgs with exactly the filters and skips `hgs test affected` printed (state::worktrees::, all state::teams::dispatcher::*, and so on): exit 0, no failures. The template's output tail shows only compilation, so no per-test lines are visible; exit 0 is the evidence.
- cargo-build --package hgs (the non-test build, without the test-only clone hook): exit 0, no warnings.
- Not run:
  - Python test_worktrees and test_mobile_worktrees_native. They never use --clone, and the non-clone path is unchanged.
  - Clippy, which the integration runs.
  - A real clone of C:\work\example
